short_description: Job stuck in pending state on the GPU partition
comments: Hello, my job has been pending for over two days and I am not sure why. Staff reply: Your job is pending because it requests 4 GPUs and a long walltime, which makes it hard to schedule. Try lowering the walltime or requesting fewer GPUs, and use squeue with the --start option to see the estimated start time. If the job is still pending after that, send us the job ID and we can look at it.

short_description: How do I load a specific Python version in a batch job
comments: Hi, I need Python 3.9 in my batch script but the default module is different. Staff reply: Use the module command to load the version you need before your python line. Run module spider python to list available versions, then add module load python/3.9 to your script before calling your program. Remember that modules loaded in an interactive session are not carried into batch jobs.

short_description: Quota exceeded error when writing to home directory
comments: I keep getting a disk quota exceeded error when I try to save files. Staff reply: Your home directory has a small fixed quota and it is currently full. Check your usage with the quota command, then move large files to your project space or scratch space. Scratch is meant for temporary data and is purged periodically, so keep important results in project space.

short_description: Cannot connect to cluster over SSH
comments: Connection timed out when I run ssh from my laptop. Staff reply: Please confirm you are using the correct login hostname and that your network or VPN is not blocking port 22. Try connecting from a different network to rule that out. If it still fails, send the exact error message and the output of ssh with the -v flag so we can see where the connection stops.

short_description: Request to install a Python package
comments: Could you install a package for me on the cluster? Staff reply: You can install most Python packages yourself in a virtual environment without needing admin help. Create one with python -m venv, activate it, and install the package with pip. If the package needs a system library or a license, let us know and we can see whether a central install makes sense.
